summary: Squaw Island Light, a brick tower lit in 1892 in Lake Michigan's Beaver Island group, was discontinued in 1928 and is privately owned.

lens.where: National Museum of the Great Lakes, Toledo, Ohio (LighthouseFriends)

structures.note: Attached to the keeper's dwelling; 11 feet square at its base

access.note: Island and lighthouse privately owned; not open to visitors (LighthouseFriends).

events.note: Brick tower and attached dwelling completed 16 September 1892
Fourth-order Fresnel lens placed in service 10 October 1892
Duplicate 10-inch steam whistles in operation from October 1892
Barn converted to a five-room residence for an assistant keeper
Keepers' boat capsized 14 December 1900; two women and assistant keeper Lucien Morden drowned
Light and fog signal discontinued after the Lansing Shoal light station went into commission on 6 October 1928
Government bids for the station property accepted at Milwaukee, April 1937 (LighthouseFriends)
Private owner replaced the roof and restored the exterior (LighthouseFriends)

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The USLHS place record gives Gladstone, Emmet County and 44.6873, -85.3128. The roster's keepers and LighthouseFriends place the station on Squaw Island in the Beaver Island group, at about 45.84, -85.59, which is the record's position. The place record's position is treated as wrong.

Squaw Point (Gladstone): the 1893 Board report (scan p.176) says an act of 15 February 1893 authorized a light on Sanders Point, or Squaw Point, to guide into Gladstone Harbor, 'but no appropriation therefor has yet been made'; the 1894 report (scan p.325) lists a 'Squaw Point (Gladstone) light, Michigan' at $5,000. Those sources place it at Gladstone, not on Squaw Island. The sources read do not say whether it was built; the story says so.

notes_for_editor: Same name: 'Squaw Point (Gladstone)' (Board reports 1893 and 1894) is a different light at Gladstone Harbor on Green Bay and is not used for this station's facts. The USLHS place record 'Squaw Island - Light Station, Gladstone, Emmet Co.' with coordinates 44.6873, -85.3128 does not match this station; the roster and LighthouseFriends match the Beaver Island station, and the record's position (45.840, -85.587) agrees with LighthouseFriends (45.8393, -85.588). The place record's location is in resolved_conflicts. Accident: the Manitowoc Pilot (20 Dec 1900, p. 5) names the second woman as 'Mrs. Davis' of Richmond, Indiana, aged 23; LighthouseFriends names her as the wife's niece, Lucy Davis. The sources conflict and this is not resolved; the story gives both. The Pilot is an OCR text: 'lust week' appears in the OCR for 'last week', so the evidence entry keeps the OCR spelling. Dates: the 1891-1894 Light-House Board reports are cited by scan page; printed pages were not confirmed. The 1899 fog-whistle figures are from the fiscal year ended 30 June 1899 and the 1900 figures from the year ended 30 June 1900. Discontinuance: the 1928 Bulletin records only the Lansing Shoal station, not the Squaw Island discontinuance. The 1928 Commissioner report is not in the corpus, so the discontinuance rests on LighthouseFriends (which also rests on Lansing Shoal). The 1936-37 divestment attempt and the 2013 sale price are LighthouseFriends only. Owner: LighthouseFriends names a private owner from 1964 and a 2016 restoration; the owner is not named in the story because the owner is a private person. Access: the story does not suggest landing on the island; LighthouseFriends' suggestion to see the lighthouse 'by landing on the island' is omitted on purpose. Name: Wikipedia calls the island 'Ojibwa Island (formerly Squaw Island)'; no primary source here confirms the rename, so the story keeps 'Squaw Island'. Keepers: 31 roster lines (USLHS). LighthouseFriends and the roster agree on the head keepers. No keeper is linked to another station. Checked in this pass: the Gladstone sentence was wrong (it said the light 'stood at a different place'); the 1893 report says no appropriation had been made, and the 1894 report lists a $5,000 item, so the story now says the sources do not say whether it was built. The 1893 completion date (16 Sept 1892) and first operation (10 Oct 1892) are on scan p.176 of the FY1893 volume, the source of footnote 4. The Pilot account is an inquest report (Coroner Luhman's jury); its headline was not read, so footnote 8 gives no headline. Its OCR reads 'Mrs. Win. Davis' and 'lust week'; the story says 'Mrs.' Davis and 'the Friday of the week before'. The USLHS place record's city (Gladstone) and coordinates are the Gladstone record's, not this station's; the roster lines match LighthouseFriends and are cited to the same record. The owner who restored the lighthouse in 2016 is named in LighthouseFriends but not in the story (a private person).
